hints.title: Whitespace Trimming and Token Reversal
hints.text: The input string may contain leading, trailing, and multiple consecutive spaces. How can parsing words from right to left naturally reverse word order without extra spaces?

hints.title: Boundary Scanning Word Token Invariant
hints.text: Scanning indices backward from end to start and identifying contiguous non-space tokens ensures words are collected in reversed sequence.

hints.title: Backward Token Assembly Procedure
hints.text: Scan the string backward. When encountering a non-space character, note the word end. Continue scanning until hitting a space or string start to find the word start. Extract the word token, add it to result tokens, and continue until all words are collected. Join tokens with single space.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Naive string concatenation without whitespace tokenization retains excess spaces and leads to quadratic string copy overhead.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Token extraction runs in linear O(N) time using O(N) memory to assemble the normalized output.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle leading spaces, trailing spaces, and multiple spaces between words cleanly.
